newsitem.title: INDIA: India electronic hardware exporters win incentives.
newsitem.headline: India electronic hardware exporters win incentives.

text.p: India said on Monday that export units manufacturing electronic hardware will be allowed to sell up to 50 percent of their annual output in the domestic market.

"Electronic hardware units can now sell up to 50 percent in domestic tariff area (DTA) on an annual basis while exporting 50 percent," the Commerce Ministry said in a statement on a five-year new export-import policy.

An electronic hardware exporter will be allowed to sell in the DTA up to 40 percent of the value of the output if the net foreign exchange earnings is more than 25 percent of the annual exports, the ministry said.
If net foreign exchange earnings are between 15 and 25 percent of total exports, up to 30 percent of the value of the total output can be sold in the DTA, it said.
No such DTA sale will be permitted if an electronic hardware maker's net foreign exchange earnings are less than 15 percent of exports, it said.
